# Two implementations, `primarycensored` and `CensoredDistributions.jl`

## Eighteen branches, or the type you passed

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```stan
real dist_lcdf(real delay, array[] real params,
               int dist_id) {
  if (dist_id == 1)
    return lognormal_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else if (dist_id == 2)
    return gamma_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  // ... 15 more branches ...
  else if (dist_id == 25)
    return von_mises_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else reject("Invalid distribution identifier: ",
              dist_id);
}
```

- And a second table of 10, saying which of those 18 have positive
  support
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```julia
primarycensored_cdf(dist::Gamma, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::LogNormal, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::Weibull, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::D1, primary_event::D2,
    x::Real, method::NumericSolver
) where {D1 <: UnivariateDistribution,
         D2 <: UnivariateDistribution}
```

- **Three closed forms** picked by the type you passed, and one
  fallback for any `UnivariateDistribution`
- `cdf(primary_censored(Frechet(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1)), 3.0)` returns
  `0.847`. Nobody wrote that. In Stan `Frechet` needs a new branch, a
  new integer and a rebuild
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
The Stan file has to know every distribution it will ever support. The
Julia file does not have to know any of them.
:::

## The distribution is built from the parameters being sampled

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
```julia
using CensoredDistributions, Distributions, Turing

@model function double_censored_model(values, weights)
    α ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    θ ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    d = double_interval_censored(
        Gamma(α, θ); upper = 15, interval = 1
    )
    values ~ weight(d, weights)
end

model = double_censored_model(values, weights)
chain = sample(model, NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 2)
```

::: {.attribution}
Model code from `CensoredDistributions.jl/README.md:71-85`, run for
this talk against v0.2.22
:::
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- In Stan `dist_id` is data, so the distribution is fixed before
  sampling starts. Here `Gamma(α, θ)` is **built out of the parameters
  being sampled**
- `primary_censored` is the $w_P$ integral, `upper` truncates at $C$,
  `interval_censored` is $w_S$, and `double_interval_censored` stacks
  all three **in that order**
:::
::::
